title: 1871 streets round the jaunt stops: wood blocks, stone walks, steps
items: The Nicholson pavement on Clark, Lake, Washington, State and Madison now reads as rows of worn pine end-grain blocks with gravel-and-tar joints, wheel-polished tracks and dung down the horse paths, instead of grey setts.

Stone-flag walks with stone kerbs stand before the fine fronts the photographs show: Lake Street, Crosby's, the Sherman House, the Court House square, the Chamber of Commerce, State Street's marble blocks and the Tribune. Other walks stay plank.
Stone crosswalks cross the paved streets round the stops; plank crossings stay on the dirt streets, and a wet gutter runs along every kerb.
Here and there a stretch of walk stands a step or two above its neighbours, Chicago's raised grade, with steps up and down that you climb as you walk.
The backs of the downtown blocks are trodden yards instead of lawn; the Court House square keeps its grass. Boulder pavement on the river streets and the dirt streets are muddier and more varied.
